caveats: AI predictions. Cross-sensor pre and post plus post-cloud can inflate destroyed calls. Coverage limited to the analyzed AOI. Field verification is the ground truth.
name: hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage
notes:
Part of the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team response activation for the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli flash flood in Nepal.

AI-scored building damage per OpenStreetMap footprint inside the SkySat post-event tile that covers the upper Trishuli / Bhote Koshi confluence around 28.24 N, 85.365 E. See the interactive overview for the pre versus post compare viewer.

For the flood-affected area boundary, OSM and Overture building inventories and the full river corridor context, download [hot_flood_npl](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl). This analysis is limited to availability of POST imagery scene and doesn't represent the full damage extent area.

Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) acts as a bridge between the traditional humanitarian responders and the OpenStreetMap Community. HOT works both remotely and physically in countries to assist the collection of geographic data, usage of that information and training others in OpenStreetMap.
